newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM Ranariddh backs trial for Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM Ranariddh backs trial for Pol Pot.

text.p: Cambodian Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Wednesday he would back any attempt to bring Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot and his most feared commander before an international tribunal.

"If someone wants to bring them to justice or the international court, I think I clearly support it," the prince said at a ceremony inducting hundreds of alleged Khmer Rouge undercover agents into the government armed forces.

Ranariddh, who backed a pardon for former Pol Pot associate Ieng Sary and has said other Khmer Rouge leaders could be forgiven if they came over to the government, said he did not know the whereabouts of Pol Pot and commander Ta Mok.
Military officials believe they are in the northern base of Anlong Veng, the last stronghold of hardliners holding out after the defection of thousands of their comrades.

The manager of the U.S.-funded Cambodian Genocide Programme said at the weekend it had discovered enough new evidence to clearly implicate Pol Pot and other Khmer Rouge leaders in crimes against humanity during their brutal 1975-79 rule.
A U.N. official said the world body was unlikely to propose a costly international trial, but individual nations could do so.

Ranariddh has previously said any deal with Pol Pot was unacceptable and analysts said that by making public his support for a trial, the prince was shutting the door on reconciliation with the two most unpalatable Khmer Rouge leaders.

Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen persuaded King Norodom Sihanouk to pardon Ieng Sary from a 1979 death sentence handed down in his absence for his role in the death of more than one million people during the Khmer Rouge rule.
"We consider the Khmer Rouge are finished," Ranariddh said at a ceremony welcoming 556 defectors into the army.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen, rivals in the coalition government, have been vying for the allegiance of Khmer Rouge defectors.
The Khmer Rouge reneged on a 1991 U.N.-sponsored peace pact and had been fighting the government set up in 1993.
